title_en: China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, Kunming Office v. Kunming Xinrenren Seafood Restaurant Co., Ltd. and Kunming Xinrenren Jinshi Restaurant Co., Ltd. — dispute over loan contract
ruling_gist_en: In civil cases, where the legal representatives of several defendant enterprise legal persons are the same individual, and their statutory duties and obligations in each enterprise legal person are substantially identical, the practice of serving legal documents such as the summons for trial to only one such enterprise legal person, and then having that enterprise legal person forward the documents to the other defendant enterprise legal persons or serving by leaving them at the premises, does not affect the litigant's procedural rights and does not constitute a violation of trial procedure.
keywords_en: civil; loan contract dispute; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Yunnan Province; legal person; contract law; legality of service procedure; validity of debt transfer; validity of mortgage guarantee; affirm original judgment; loan contract; assignment of creditor's rights; mortgage guarantee; joint and several guarantee; contract dispute; limited liability company loan contract dispute
full_text_en:
China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation Kunming Office v. Kunming Xinrenren Seafood Restaurant Co., Ltd. and Kunming Xinrenren Jinshi Restaurant Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Loan Contract

【Ruling Summary】

In the trial of civil cases, when several corporate legal persons as defendants have the same legal representative, and the statutory powers and obligations of that legal representative in each corporate legal person are substantially identical, the practice of serving court documents such as summons for hearing to only one of the corporate legal persons, and then either forwarding them through that corporate legal person to the other corporate legal persons or leaving them at that location, does not affect the litigant's procedural rights and does not constitute a violation of trial procedure.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2007) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 210

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Kunming Xinrenren Seafood Restaurant Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 611 Huancheng West Road, Kunming City, Yunnan Province.
Legal Representative: Pan Fusong, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Hu Yupeng, lawyer at Beijing Boyu Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation Kunming Office, domiciled at No. 315 Renmin West Road, Kunming City, Yunnan Province.
Responsible Person: Xu Ximin, General Manager of the Office.
Agent ad litem: Yang Hong, lawyer at Beijing Jintai Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Kunming Xinrenren Jinshi Restaurant Co., Ltd., domiciled at Jinshi Road, Jinshi Residential Area, Kunming City, Yunnan Province.
Legal Representative: Pan Fusong, General Manager of the Company.

The appellant, Kunming Xinrenren Seafood Restaurant Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Seafood Restaurant), having appealed against the Civil Judgment (2006) Yun Gao Min Er Chu Zi No. 25-3 rendered by the Yunnan High People's Court in the case of the loan contract dispute with the appellees, China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation Kunming Office (hereinafter referred to as Great Wall Kunming Office) and Kunming Xinrenren Jinshi Restaurant Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinshi Restaurant), filed an appeal to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Jin Jianfeng, Judge Wang Dongmin, and Acting Judge Yin Yuan to hear the case, with Court Clerk Zhao Suijun keeping the record. The trial of this case has now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial: Between January 1998 and December 2001, Seafood Restaurant borrowed a total of RMB 19 million from the Kunming City Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China in four separate loans. On December 31, 2001, Seafood Restaurant borrowed a total of RMB 10.7 million from the Huguo Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China in two separate loans. On October 12, 1999, Seafood Restaurant issued a "Guarantee Commitment Letter" to the Fumin County Sub-branch of the Agricultural Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Fumin County ABC), undertaking to provide a guarantee for a loan of RMB 3.5 million borrowed by Fumin Yuebao Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuebao Company) from Fumin County ABC on December 23, 1997, with the guarantee period ending on December 30, 2001. If Yuebao Company was unable to repay the loan at maturity, Seafood Restaurant agreed to repay the loan principal and interest on behalf of Yuebao Company. Subsequently, Yuebao Company repaid RMB 200,000 of the loan principal. On October 30, 2001, Seafood Restaurant again issued a "Guarantee Commitment Letter" to Fumin County ABC, undertaking to continue providing a guarantee for the extended loan of RMB 3.3 million borrowed by Yuebao Company from Fumin County ABC, and assuming joint and several liability and repayment responsibility.

Pursuant to the Notice on Printing and Distributing the Provisions on Fiscal and Financial Policies Concerning Financial Asset Management Companies (Cai Zhai Zi [2000] No. 102) and the Supplementary Notice on Issues Concerning Capital Transfer of Asset Management Companies (Cai Jin [2000] No. 44) of the Ministry of Finance, the Agricultural Bank of China and China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation jointly issued the Reply on Acceptance and Transfer of Capital Investments (Zhong Chang Zi Han [2001] No. 813) and the Notice on Issues Concerning Transfer of Capital Investments (Zhong Chang Zi Fa [2003] No. 22). In accordance with these two documents, the Provincial Agricultural Bank transferred (i.e., assigned) the principal of the creditor's right of RMB 33 million, which it held against Seafood Restaurant, to Great Wall Kunming Office as a capital transfer, which was approved. On December 30, 2001, the Provincial Agricultural Bank, the plaintiff (Great Wall Kunming Office), and Seafood Restaurant entered into an "Agreement" stipulating that all of the above RMB 33 million creditor's rights held by the Provincial Agricultural Bank against the defendant Seafood Restaurant were transferred to Great Wall Kunming Office.

On March 18, 2003, in order to further clarify the repayment of the debt, Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company jointly entered into a "Debt Agreement" with Great Wall Kunming Office, which mainly stipulated: Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company shall jointly serve as the debtors and bear the obligation to repay all debts to Great Wall Kunming Office; the loan term was adjusted to six years, i.e., from January 1, 2002 to December 31, 2007; the repayment period provided for annual repayment of the debt principal to Great Wall Kunming Office, i.e., repayment of RMB 4 million in 2003, RMB 4.5 million in 2004, RMB 5 million in 2005, RMB 8 million in 2006, and RMB 11.5 million in 2007. In addition, Article 9, paragraph 3 and Article 11, paragraph 1 of the Agreement also specified that Great Wall Kunming Office, in order to ensure the security, profitability and liquidity of the creditor's rights, had the right to recover the principal and interest of the creditor's rights within the prescribed period or in advance; if any one of the four parties (the plaintiff, Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company) violated any provision of the Agreement, the other party had the right to take corresponding protective measures in accordance with the law. On the same day, Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company also jointly entered into a "Mortgage (Guarantee) Contract" with Great Wall Kunming Office, stipulating: In order to ensure the performance of the repayment obligations under the Debt Agreement, Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company were willing to assume joint and several guarantee liability for the debts owed to Great Wall Kunming Office; at the same time, Seafood Restaurant voluntarily mortgaged the property located at Blocks C, 1st-3rd floors, 1151 square meters, No. 611-613 Huancheng West Road, Kunming City (Title Certificate No. 200204922) and the ancillary building at No. 611-613 Huancheng West Road, 1151 square meters (Title Certificate No. 9803122) to provide mortgage security for the debts under the Debt Agreement. Great Wall Kunming Office, Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company also notarized the Debt Agreement and the Mortgage (Guarantee) Contract at the Kunming Notary Public Office on October 8, 2003. On October 13, 2003, Great Wall Kunming Office and Seafood Restaurant registered the mortgage for the property used as collateral with the Kunming Real Estate Administration Bureau, and Great Wall Kunming Office received the "House Other Rights Certificates" numbered Kunming Shi Fang Ta Zi No. 200312775 and 200312776 issued by the registration authority.

Because Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company did not perform their repayment obligations as agreed in the Debt Agreement, Great Wall Kunming Office entered into a "Supplementary Agreement" with Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company on August 12, 2005, stipulating: Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company confirmed the RMB 33 million creditor's rights transferred from the Provincial Agricultural Bank to Great Wall Kunming Office, and amended the repayment period to one year, i.e., from September 21, 2005 to September 20, 2006. Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company must repay all loan principal and interest to Great Wall Kunming Office before the repayment deadline. If, during the agreed repayment period, Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company failed to pay interest in accordance with the prevailing loan interest rate for two consecutive quarters, Great Wall Kunming Office had the right to recover all loan principal and interest in advance.

On January 6, 2004, July 13, 2004, December 21, 2004, June 21, 2005, and December 31, 2005, Great Wall Kunming Office made five successive demands for repayment to Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company. During the collection period by Great Wall Kunming Office, from September 21, 2005 to December 21, 2005, Seafood Restaurant defaulted on the quarterly interest of RMB 465,465; from December 22, 2005 to July 31, 2006, the quarterly interest payable was RMB 1,119,974.80, of which only RMB 720,000 was paid, leaving a balance of RMB 399,974.80 unpaid. As of July 31, 2006, the defendants Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company owed a total loan principal of RMB 33 million, interest and penalty interest of RMB 4,293,247.69, totaling RMB 37,293,247.69. After repeated demands went unanswered, Great Wall Kunming Office filed the lawsuit with the court.

The court of first instance held: The "Agreement" entered into by the Provincial Agricultural Bank, Great Wall Kunming Office, and Seafood Restaurant, as well as the "Debt Agreement", "Supplementary Agreement", and "Mortgage (Guarantee) Contract" entered into by Great Wall Kunming Office with Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company were voluntarily concluded in accordance with national laws and relevant policies; they represent the true intentions of the parties, and the parties to the Mortgage (Guarantee) Contract also registered the mortgage with the real estate registration authority. Thus, the above four contracts are lawful and valid. The RMB 33 million creditor's rights transferred from the Provincial Agricultural Bank to Great Wall Kunming Office as agreed in the "Agreement" consisted of RMB 29.7 million borrowed by Seafood Restaurant from the Agricultural Bank and RMB 3.3 million in guarantee debt for Yuebao Company. When signing the "Agreement", Seafood Restaurant voluntarily acted as a debtor to repay the RMB 3.3 million debt borrowed by Yuebao Company from Fumin County ABC; this act did not violate national laws or administrative regulations, and should be permitted. When signing the "Debt Agreement" and "Supplementary Agreement", Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company confirmed the above transferred RMB 33 million creditor's rights and voluntarily acted as joint debtors to repay the said RMB 33 million debt; this act also did not violate national laws or administrative regulations, and should be permitted. After the above four contracts were signed, all parties should have actively performed their obligations in accordance with the terms of the contracts. However, Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company did not repay the RMB 33 million debt by the final repayment deadline set in the last signed "Supplementary Agreement", i.e., before September 20, 2006, nor did they pay interest in full on a quarterly basis. Their conduct constituted a breach of contract, and they should bear corresponding liability for breach. Great Wall Kunming Office acquired the RMB 33 million creditor's rights in this case through assignment from the Provincial Agricultural Bank, and it has the right to assert its claims against the debtors Seafood Restaurant, Jinshi Restaurant, and Youyicun Company. In this case, Great Wall Kunming Office chose not to sue Youyicun Company and only sued Seafood Restaurant and Jinshi Restaurant, which is an exercise of its discretionary right, and the court permitted it. In this case, Great Wall Kunming Office's claim that the defendants Seafood Restaurant and Jinshi Restaurant should bear the responsibility of repaying the loan principal and interest and that it should be allowed to enforce its mortgage rights is supported by facts and law, and the court upheld it. In view of the fact that the final repayment period under the contracts has expired, the "Debt Agreement" and "Supplementary Agreement" signed by the parties have naturally expired due to the expiration of the performance period; there is no issue of rescission. The only issue in this case is whether the parties performed the contracts as agreed and whether there was a breach. Therefore, Great Wall Kunming Office's request to rescind the "Debt Agreement" and "Supplementary Agreement" is practically unnecessary. In addition, since Great Wall Kunming Office failed to submit evidence of the lawyer's fees it paid, the court did not support its claim that the defendants should bear the costs incurred for realizing the creditor's rights. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 108 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, Article 60, paragraph 1, Articles 206 and 207 of the Contract Law of the PRC, and Article 53 of the Security Law of the PRC, the court ruled as follows: 1. The defendants Kunming Xinrenren Seafood Restaurant Co., Ltd. and Kunming Xinrenren Jinshi Restaurant Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, repay the plaintiff China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation Kunming Office the loan principal of RMB 33 million, the interest and penalty interest of RMB 4,293,247.69 as of July 31, 2006, totaling RMB 37,293,247.69, plus interest and penalty interest from August 1, 2006 until full repayment (interest and penalty interest shall be calculated at the overdue loan interest rate prescribed by the People's Bank of China for the same period); 2. If the defendants Kunming Xinrenren Seafood Restaurant Co., Ltd. and Kunming Xinrenren Jinshi Restaurant Co., Ltd. fail to repay the above loan and interest, the plaintiff China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation Kunming Office may have priority in receiving compensation from the proceeds of the collateral property of the defendant Kunming Xinrenren Seafood Restaurant Co., Ltd., i.e., the properties located at Blocks C, 1st-3rd floors, No. 611-613 Huancheng West Road, Kunming City, with Title Certificate Nos. 200204922 and 9803122, by way of discount, auction, or sale. 3. The other claims of the plaintiff China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation Kunming Office are dismissed. Court acceptance fee of RMB 99,739.45, property preservation fee of RMB 27,760, and appraisal fee of RMB 1,500 shall be borne jointly by the defendants Kunming Xinrenren Seafood Restaurant Co., Ltd. and Kunming Xinrenren Jinshi Restaurant Co., Ltd.

Seafood Restaurant, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, stating: 1. The first-instance trial procedure was unlawful. During the first-instance trial, the first-instance court, on February 28, 2007, served on the appellant litigation documents for evidence exchange on April 2, 2007 and court hearing on April 3, 2007, and requested the appellant to forward the said litigation documents to the other two defendants in this case (i.e., Kunming Xinrenren Jinshi Restaurant Co., Ltd. and Kunming Xinrenren Youyicun Catering Co., Ltd.). After the appellant explicitly stated that it was unable to forward the said hearing documents, the first-instance court left the said hearing documents at the appellant's place and deemed this as service on the other two defendants. On April 2, 2007, the appellant filed a written objection with the first-instance court. The appellant argued that the defendant at first instance, Jinshi Restaurant, and the defendant at first instance, Xinrenren Youyicun Catering Co., Ltd., were independent legal persons with different investors and legal person asset structures; their registered addresses and business premises were not the same as the appellant's registered address and business premises. The first-instance court's act of leaving the litigation documents at the appellant's place and deeming this as service on the other two defendants was clearly improper, deprived the litigants of their procedural rights, and also deprived the appellant of the opportunity to cross-examine and differentiate on substantive issues with the other defendants in this case, and affected the judge's review and judgment of the entire case. 2. The first-instance judgment's determination that the contracts involved in this case were valid was clearly erroneous. The court of first instance held that the "Agreement" entered into by the Provincial Agricultural Bank, the appellant, and the appellee, as well as the "Debt Agreement", "Supplementary Agreement", and "Mortgage (Guarantee) Contract" entered into by the appellant and the appellee were valid, which was obviously biased. On December 30, 2001, the Provincial Agricultural Bank, the appellant, and the appellee signed an agreement, Article 3 of which stipulated: "If Party B and Party C (i.e., the appellant and Great Wall) agree to cooperate and restructure the company... then the creditor's rights of approximately RMB 33 million will be transferred from Party A to Party B." It can be seen that this agreement is a legal act conditioned upon the condition that the appellant and Great Wall Kunming Office "agree to cooperate and restructure the company." During the performance of this agreement, Great Wall Kunming Office refused to restructure the appellant on the grounds that the appellant paid less investment profit, and thus the condition for the agreement to take effect was lost. The "Debt Agreement", "Supplementary Agreement", and "Mortgage (Guarantee) Contract" subsequently signed by the appellant and the appellee Great Wall Kunming Office should be deemed invalid. On November 10, 2000, Article 2 of the State Council's "Regulations on Financial Asset Management Companies" clearly stipulates: Financial asset management companies are wholly state-owned banking financial institutions established by decision of the State Council to acquire non-performing loans from state-owned banks, and to manage and dispose of the assets formed from the acquisition of non-performing loans from state-owned banks. Article 10 stipulates that financial asset management companies shall conduct business activities within the scope of the non-performing loans they have acquired from state-owned banks. However, the loans involved in this case, when they were with the Provincial Agricultural Bank, were managed as normal loans of the Agricultural Bank. According to the five-category loan classification management method, these loans were not non-performing loans. Therefore, Great Wall Kunming Office's acquisition and disposal of these loans are invalid acts.

The appellee, Great Wall Company Kunming Office, argued in its defense: 1. The court of first instance committed no procedural violation in the trial of this case. During the trial by the court of first instance, the appellant, the Seafood Restaurant, in order to continue occupying state-owned assets for business operations and obtaining profits, intentionally delayed the proceedings and exploited legal loopholes, making a big issue over procedure. Despite knowing that the court of first instance had full jurisdiction, it raised an objection to jurisdiction to delay the trial. After the court of first instance rejected its objection to jurisdiction, it appealed to the Supreme People's Court, which clearly demonstrated its intent and attempt to delay the proceedings. Even after the Supreme People's Court likewise rejected the appellant Seafood Restaurant's appeal against the jurisdiction objection, after the court of first instance lawfully served the appellant with the summons, evidence exchange, and other relevant procedural documents, when the court conducted a public hearing on April 2, 2007, the appellant and its authorized representatives failed to appear in court without justifiable reasons. After completely failing to comply with the trial schedule and disrespecting the court proceedings, the appellant once again resorted to the same trick and openly requested the court of second instance to "remand the case for retrial" on the grounds of "procedural violations in the judgment of first instance" and "deprivation of the litigant's procedural rights." This shows the extent to which the appellant has gone to delay the proceedings. 2. The determination by the judgment of first instance regarding the nature of the contracts involved in this case fully complies with the law and is in no way improper. The "Agreement" signed among the Yunnan Provincial Agricultural Bank, the appellee, and the appellant, as well as the "Debt Agreement," the "Supplemental Agreement," and the "Mortgage (Guarantee) Contract" signed between the appellee and the appellant, were all voluntarily entered into by the parties, representing their true intentions. The contents of the agreements and contracts do not violate national laws or relevant policy provisions. The mortgaged property involved in the "Mortgage (Guarantee) Contract" was also lawfully registered with the registration authorities. Therefore, the court of first instance's determination that the four contracts involved in this case are lawful and valid fully complies with the law, and there is no issue of "obvious impropriety." After the appellant performed its obligation to repay part of the loan interest to the appellee in accordance with the "Debt Agreement," it subsequently refused to repay the loan principal and interest to the appellee on time as stipulated in the debt agreement. After the appellee's repeated demands for payment proved fruitless, the appellee, in order to protect its rights and interests from further infringement by the appellant, filed a lawsuit with the people's court in accordance with the law. Therefore, the appellant's breach of contract in failing to pay interest as agreed, which led the appellee to bring the lawsuit, is sophistically argued by the appellant as an invalid act of the appellee refusing to restructure the company because it considered the investment profit to be too low. The appellant has truly resorted to all means to achieve its goals. In summary, the judgment of first instance, whether in procedure or substance, complies with the law and is in no way improper. The appellant, having not participated in the substantive trial of the case, has raised its appeal requests, facts, and grounds for the purpose of achieving its illegal objectives, which are utterly unfounded. Therefore, the appellee requests that the people's court of second instance, based on the facts found, dismiss the appellant's appeal in accordance with the law and uphold the objective and fair judgment of the court of first instance.

The appellee, Jinshi Restaurant, did not submit a defense.

The facts found by this court are essentially consistent with those found by the court of first instance.

This court holds that: The legal representatives of the Seafood Restaurant and the Jinshi Restaurant are the same person, and the statutory functions, powers, and obligations of the legal representatives of the two companies are basically the same. Therefore, the court of first instance's service of legal documents such as the summons on the Seafood Restaurant, followed by forwarding them to the Jinshi Restaurant or leaving them at the premises, did not affect the litigant's procedural rights, nor did it cause any harm to the litigant's substantive rights. The appellant's ground of appeal regarding "procedural violations in the trial" is untenable and is dismissed by this court.

The "Agreement" signed among the Yunnan Provincial Agricultural Bank, the Great Wall Company Kunming Office, and the Seafood Restaurant, as well as the "Debt Agreement," the "Supplemental Agreement," and the "Mortgage (Guarantee) Contract" signed between the Great Wall Company Kunming Office and the Seafood Restaurant and the Jinshi Restaurant, represent the true intentions of the parties. They confirmed the assignment of the RMB 33,000,000 creditor's right, and the Seafood Restaurant and the Jinshi Restaurant jointly promised to repay the above debts. At the same time, mortgage registration was completed in accordance with the "Mortgage (Guarantee) Contract." The above contracts comply with the provisions of China's laws and regulations, and their contents are lawful and valid. This court confirms them. After the above four contracts were concluded and became effective, the Seafood Restaurant and the Jinshi Restaurant did not repay the debts or pay interest within the repayment period stipulated in the final "Supplemental Agreement" signed by the parties. They have thus constituted a breach of contract and shall bear liability for breach of contract. The Great Wall Company Kunming Office is entitled to assert its rights against the debtors, the Seafood Restaurant and the Jinshi Restaurant. Its claim that the Seafood Restaurant and the Jinshi Restaurant should bear the responsibility for repaying the loan principal and interest and its claim for enforcement of the mortgage are supported by this court. The appeal requests of the Seafood Restaurant lack factual and legal basis and are dismissed by this court. The judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this court hereby rules as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The case acceptance fee for the second instance, RMB 99,739.45, shall be borne by Kunming Xinrenren Seafood Restaurant Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Jin Jianfeng

Judge: Wang Dongmin

Acting Judge: Yin Yuan

December 22, 2007

Clerk: Zhao Suijun
